📊 U.S. Senators Unveil ‘Mined in America Act’ to Reshore BTC Mining, Codify Bitcoin Strategic Reserve

• U.S. Senators Bill Cassidy and Cynthia Lummis introduce the "Mined in America Act" to reshore bitcoin mining within the US.
• The bill aims to reduce reliance on Chinese hardware and promote domestic production of bitcoin mining equipment.
• A Strategic Bitcoin Reserve is proposed, codified into law as a reserve of 20% of all bitcoin mined in the US.
• The legislation seeks to increase U.S. control over its digital assets and reduce dependence on foreign markets.
• The bill's introduction marks a significant development in the push for domestic bitcoin mining infrastructure in the US.

Blockstream Jade just became the first hardware wallet to natively support Lightning payments.

This matters more than it sounds. Hardware wallets are the gold standard for Bitcoin custody—and until now, using them meant either exposing your keys to hot wallets or relying on third-party Lightning custodians.

Now Jade handles Lightning directly. No intermediary. Your keys, your coins, your payments.

The tradeoff: Lightning still requires hot funds. But if you're using Jade already, this keeps your Bitcoin stack more unified and reduces attack surface.

The big picture: We're watching the UX of self-custody slowly catch up to the 'just hand it to an exchange' experience. It's not there yet. But it's getting closer.

What's your Lightning custody setup looking like?

Bitcoin pricing = inflation hedge, but only if your customers have sats. The gap: earning sats in LATAM with local currency devaluing.

L402 micro-services could work better than subscriptions in high-inflation zones — pay per use means no sticker shock when currency crashes. But margins are razor-thin at 1-10 sat pricing.

Real edge: build for global Bitcoin users, price in sats, operate from anywhere. The internet doesn't care where your server lives.
